data.title: Ituran Location and Control Ltd. (NASDAQ:ITRN) Analysts Are Pretty Bullish On The Stock After Recent Results
data.description:
Last week saw the newest quarterly earnings release from Ituran Location and Control Ltd. (NASDAQ:ITRN), an important milestone in the company's journey to build a stronger business. Ituran Location and Control reported in line with analyst predictions, delivering revenues of US$107m and statutory earnings per share of US$0.91, suggesting the business is executing well and in line with its plan. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Ituran Location and Control's twin analysts is for revenues of US$440.7m in 2027. This reflects a notable 8.1% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to grow 17% to US$4.00. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of US$440.7m and earnings per share (EPS) of US$3.54 in 2027. There was no real change to the revenue estimates, but the analysts do seem more bullish on earnings, given the nice increase in earnings per share expectations following these results.

Check out our latest analysis for Ituran Location and Control

The consensus price target rose 17% to US$74.50, suggesting that higher earnings estimates flow through to the stock's valuation as well.

Another way we can view these estimates is in the context of the bigger picture, such as how the forecasts stack up against past performance, and whether forecasts are more or less bullish relative to other companies in the industry. The period to the end of 2027 brings more of the same, according to the analysts, with revenue forecast to display 6.5% growth on an annualised basis. That is in line with its 7.6% annual growth over the past five years. Compare this with the broader industry (in aggregate), which analyst estimates suggest will see revenues grow 14% annually. So although Ituran Location and Control is expected to maintain its revenue growth rate, it's forecast to grow slower than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest takeaway for us is the consensus earnings per share upgrade, which suggests a clear improvement in sentiment around Ituran Location and Control's earnings potential next year. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. There was also a nice increase in the price target, with the analysts clearly feeling that the intrinsic value of the business is improving.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. We have analyst estimates for Ituran Location and Control going out as far as 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

data.title: Missed Coca-Cola's Run? Here's What Early Buyers Saw
data.description:
If you had bought Coca-Cola on 1 January 2026 and simply sat tight, the outcome would look very different in your portfolio today. Holding Coca-Cola from the start of the year would have returned 43.9%, including dividends. The puzzle is what early buyers were really weighing back then. Were they more focused on the long-running IRS tax dispute or on concerns that a mature soda franchise might struggle to find new growth engines?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

The easy part of this move is behind Coca-Cola. Zero in on 37 high quality undervalued stocks for companies trading below our estimates.

The Two Stories Coca-Cola Investors Were Really Arguing About

The shares cost US$69.91 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at Coca-Cola then had to decide whether the business still deserved a premium tag or whether the valuation was stretched for a mature drinks group.

The bullish Narrative saw upside. It put Fair Value at US$78.85, 13% above the start price, and leaned on expectations that emerging market demand, digital ordering and value-added dairy like fairlife could support higher revenue and fatter margins.

The bearish Narrative pointed lower. It set Fair Value at US$54.61, 22% below the start price. This view focused on Coca-Cola’s reliance on carbonated soft drinks and argued that limited traction in newer categories and a future P/E assumption of 22.0x left little room for disappointment.

What The Coca-Cola Results Actually Tested

Coca-Cola’s Q3 2026 report, with revenue at US$13.38b versus US$12.46b a year earlier and net income at US$4.01b versus US$3.70b, leaned toward the bullish case that expected higher sales and fatter margins. Net margin edged up from 29.7% to 30.0%. The unresolved IRS tax dispute still gave the cautious view something to hold on to, so the evidence cut both ways.

The clear hinge here was whether Coca-Cola could grow earnings while holding or improving profitability. For any other stock, track revenue, absolute profit and net margin together to see if the story you are buying is actually showing up in the reported numbers.

What Coca-Cola's Current Price Already Assumes

Coca-Cola now trades at US$97.59, well above where this year began. The selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that quote, according to Jades, a Simply Wall St Community investor who wrote the Narrative, even though the business description leans heavily on the strength of the underlying franchise.

Jades frames Coca-Cola as a capital-light toll bridge on global thirst, powered by concentrate sales, pricing and mix shift. If today’s price assumes this model keeps compounding smoothly, how does the risk of slower volume in mature markets or health-related pressure interact with that expectation?

"This “system” approach keeps capital light, generates massive free cash flow (over $11 billion adjusted in 2025), and supports consistent dividends (2.66% yield currently). It is like owning a toll bridge everyone pays to cross for refreshment."

data.title: Results: Embecta Corp. Beat Earnings Expectations And Analysts Now Have New Forecasts
data.description:
As you might know, Embecta Corp. (NASDAQ:EMBC) just kicked off its latest annual results with some very strong numbers. The company beat forecasts, with revenue of US$1.1b, some 2.8% above estimates, and statutory earnings per share (EPS) coming in at US$2.15, 82% ahead of expectations. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on Embecta after the latest results.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Embecta's four analysts is for revenues of US$1.08b in 2027. This reflects a reasonable 2.7% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are forecast to plunge 36% to US$1.49 in the same period. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of US$1.08b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$1.38 in 2027. The analysts seems to have become more bullish on the business, judging by their new earnings per share estimates.

View our latest analysis for Embecta

The average the analysts price target fell 50% to US$4.00, suggesting thatthe analysts have other concerns, and the improved earnings per share outlook was not enough to allay them. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic Embecta analyst has a price target of US$5.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$3.00. These price targets show that analysts do have some differing views on the business, but the estimates do not vary enough to suggest to us that some are betting on wild success or utter failure.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the Embecta's past performance and to peers in the same industry. For example, we noticed that Embecta's rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with revenues forecast to exhibit 2.7% growth to the end of 2027 on an annualised basis. That is well above its historical decline of 2.1% a year over the past five years. Compare this against analyst estimates for the broader industry, which suggest that (in aggregate) industry revenues are expected to grow 7.4% annually for the foreseeable future. Although Embecta's revenues are expected to improve, it seems that the analysts are still bearish on the business, forecasting it to grow slower than the broader industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing here is that the analysts upgraded their earnings per share estimates, suggesting that there has been a clear increase in optimism towards Embecta following these results. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. Furthermore, the analysts also cut their price targets, suggesting that the latest news has led to greater pessimism about the intrinsic value of the business.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have estimates - from multiple Embecta analysts - going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

However, before you get too enthused, we've discovered 4 warning signs for Embecta (3 are a bit concerning!) that you should be aware of.

data.title: Why Southern Copper's Strong Quarter Could Steer Investors To ETFs
data.description:
You can own Southern Copper directly, or you can hold it as one slice of a broader fund. Holding just the single stock means living with company specific issues from Simply Wall St such as an unstable dividend track record, or the risk that profitability and free cash flow may not stay at recent levels. Owning Southern Copper inside a fund spreads those business specific swings across other holdings, and also dilutes both the downside and the upside that comes from this one miner.

Fresh results give you something concrete to weigh here. On 25 November 2026, Southern Copper reported third quarter net sales of US$4.7b and raised its copper production outlook for 2026 to 918,000 tonnes, which points to a busier future for its mines and smelters. That update, plus the new cash and stock dividend, is what you would be plugging into your portfolio if you owned shares directly or through EPU, COPX or ICOP.

Would you rather build your own basket around Southern Copper? Explore 16 top copper producer stocks.

iShares MSCI Peru and Global Exposure ETF (EPU)

Credicorp leads this portfolio and pulls a lot of EPU toward Peruvian banking and financial services, rather than metals alone. Gold producers such as Compañía de Minas Buenaventura add another slice of mining alongside copper. Southern Copper is still a major piece of what you own. It sits as the second largest holding at 21.45% of the fund, so each US$1,000 in EPU puts about US$214 into Southern Copper and the rest into other Peru linked businesses across banks, gold and broader metals.

Southern Copper’s unstable dividend record is one clear risk if you only hold the stock. EPU keeps that company specific issue in check by pairing the miner with large financial holdings like Credicorp, whose earnings and payouts lean on banking and credit demand rather than copper markets. The rest of the mix across diversified metals and distributors means this ETF gives you Southern Copper plus exposure to banks, gold and other industries that the stock alone cannot provide.

Not every stock inside EPU is priced the same way. Find out how many of EPU's holdings look undervalued.

Global X Copper Miners ETF (COPX)

COPX keeps Southern Copper to 4.5% of the portfolio, so each US$1,000 only puts about US$45 into this one miner and leaves most of your result driven by other holdings. The mix is heavy on Diversified Metals and Mining at 52.4% and Copper at 43.9%, with a small slice in Gold. BHP Group and Boliden together hold a noticeable share at the top, which steers a lot of the copper and broader mining exposure even though no single stock dominates the fund.

One risk around Southern Copper is that higher copper volumes could help keep revenue and earnings firmer than a very cautious share price view allows. COPX still revolves around copper and diversified miners, so that kind of surprise in the metal and its producers would echo across many of its holdings, which leaves you less exposed to Southern Copper alone but not insulated from how copper mining as a whole performs.

See how COPX's returns compare with the market, from one week to five years

iShares Copper and Metals Mining ETF (ICOP)

COPX and ICOP hold a similar slice of Southern Copper, with ICOP putting 4.65% of its money into the miner, so each US$1,000 means roughly US$46 tied to this one stock and the rest driven by other positions. ICOP leans on Diversified Metals and Mining at 48.1%, Copper at 36.1% and Gold at 12.2%. Anglo American and Grupo México de together hold 17.9% of the fund, which pulls more of your outcome toward large global miners that COPX does not emphasise as heavily, even though about 59% of ICOP overlaps COPX.

One risk with Southern Copper is that current profitability and free cash flow might not be unusually high after all, which would challenge any thesis built on those numbers fading. ICOP holds a wider mix of producers, so any reassessment of profit sustainability at Southern Copper alone is softened by Anglo American, Grupo México de and others that depend on different mine sets and regions. You are still heavily tied to metals and mining though, so your result depends on how this broader group of miners handles its own costs and copper demand over time.

See what you'd actually own if you bought ICOP, from its 80 positions to how much sits in the top 10.

Choosing your Southern Copper exposure

Think about what you want Southern Copper to be inside your portfolio. EPU makes it a central bet. Around US$1,000 in EPU means roughly US$214 in the miner, plus a heavy tilt to Peruvian banks and a fee of US$59 a year on a US$10,000 investment. COPX and ICOP treat Southern Copper more as a supporting position at about US$45 to US$46 per US$1,000, with the real choice between them being breadth and cost.

COPX is more concentrated at 47 holdings and charges US$65 on US$10,000. ICOP owns 80 stocks and is cheapest at US$47. After those strong recent results, you decide whether you want Southern Copper mostly paired with banks or with a wider group of miners, and how comfortable you are with an uneven stream of dividends along the way.

Credicorp alone makes up 25.17% of EPU, so how it's priced matters to anyone holding the fund. Check whether Credicorp trades above or below its fair value.

data.title: Did Record WOW Membership Just Shift Coupang (CPNG) Stock Narrative?
data.description:
• Coupang reported WOW membership in Korea at the highest level in its history and 7.5% revenue growth for the quarter ending September 2026, despite continuing to post an operating loss.
  • The combination of record WOW engagement and improving top line performance gives investors more data on how Coupang’s membership flywheel is affecting core commerce economics.

Compare Coupang’s WOW driven story with other e-commerce and retail platforms that screen well for quality and valuation by running a focused search through 37 high quality undervalued stocks in minutes.

Coupang Investment Narrative Recap

To own Coupang, you need to believe that WOW membership and customer spending patterns eventually outweigh the current operating loss. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St expects technology, automation, and Taiwan to improve earnings power over time. The recent 8.6% share price move and 7.5% revenue growth update do not materially change that in the near term. The key short term catalyst is still evidence of margin progress in the upcoming Q4 2026 results.

The biggest risk remains heavy investment in Developing Offerings, especially Taiwan, and elevated tech and logistics costs. If these outlays do not translate into better unit economics, losses could persist and push back any profitability timeline. Regulatory and operational shocks in Korea, which already hosts the data breach fine and Incheon fire, also continue to hang over the business.

The most relevant piece of information in this context is management’s comment that WOW membership in Korea is at a record high. That matters because higher engagement has historically lined up with stronger revenue per customer and deeper wallet share, which are core to the membership flywheel idea investors are considering with Coupang.

If WOW members keep spending more, it gives the Product Commerce segment a larger base to absorb fixed logistics and technology costs. That could make any improvement in automation, AI, and fulfillment efficiency show up more clearly in margins when Q4 2026 numbers arrive. It also helps offset the current EBITDA losses in Taiwan and other Developing Offerings, which the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights as a key swing factor for the overall story.

What The Current Coupang Forecasts Assume

data.description:
Vishay Intertechnology, Inc. (NYSE:VSH) stock is about to trade ex-dividend in 4 days. The ex-dividend date is one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date for shareholders to be present on the company's books to be eligible for a dividend payment. The ex-dividend date is important as the process of settlement involves a full business day. So if you miss that date, you would not show up on the company's books on the record date. Meaning, you will need to purchase Vishay Intertechnology's shares before the 2nd of December to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 15th of December.

The company's upcoming dividend is US$0.10 a share, following on from the last 12 months, when the company distributed a total of US$0.40 per share to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that Vishay Intertechnology has a trailing yield of 1.8% on the current share price of US$22.85. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether Vishay Intertechnology's dividend is reliable and sustainable. So we need to investigate whether Vishay Intertechnology can afford its dividend, and if the dividend could grow.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Dividends are usually paid out of company profits, so if a company pays out more than it earned then its dividend is usually at greater risk of being cut. Vishay Intertechnology paid out more than half (59%) of its earnings last year, which is a regular payout ratio for most companies. That said, even highly profitable companies sometimes might not generate enough cash to pay the dividend, which is why we should always check if the dividend is covered by cash flow. Fortunately, it paid out only 48% of its free cash flow in the past year.

It's encouraging to see that the dividend is covered by both profit and cash flow. This generally suggests the dividend is sustainable, as long as earnings don't drop precipitously.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with falling earnings are riskier for dividend shareholders. If earnings decline and the company is forced to cut its dividend, investors could watch the value of their investment go up in smoke. Vishay Intertechnology's earnings per share have fallen at approximately 6.1% a year over the previous five years. When earnings per share fall, the maximum amount of dividends that can be paid also falls.

Vishay Intertechnology also issued more than 5% of its market cap in new stock during the past year, which we feel is likely to hurt its dividend prospects in the long run. It's hard to grow dividends per share when a company keeps creating new shares.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. In the past 10 years, Vishay Intertechnology has increased its dividend at approximately 4.8% a year on average. That's interesting, but the combination of a growing dividend despite declining earnings can typically only be achieved by paying out more of the company's profits. This can be valuable for shareholders, but it can't go on forever.

Final Takeaway

Is Vishay Intertechnology an attractive dividend stock, or better left on the shelf? The payout ratios are within a reasonable range, implying the dividend may be sustainable. Declining earnings are a serious concern, however, and could pose a threat to the dividend in future. Overall, it's not a bad combination, but we feel that there are likely more attractive dividend prospects out there.

With that being said, if dividends aren't your biggest concern with Vishay Intertechnology, you should know about the other risks facing this business. For example, we've found 3 warning signs for Vishay Intertechnology that we recommend you consider before investing in the business.
